title: Set.Subtract always scans the argument set, so subtracting a huge set from a small one is needlessly slow

source.license_note: Real upstream victoria optimization PR #9634; measured-speedup task.

task.summary: Speed up (*Set).Subtract in lib/uint64set: it always iterates over the argument set a and calls Del on s for every element, which is wasteful when a is far larger than s.
task.instructions: Optimize the lib/uint64set package for speed WITHOUT changing behavior. The benchmark BenchmarkSubtract measures it; existing tests must still pass.
task.acceptance_notes: Behavior preserved (go test passes); higher measured speedup is better. Do NOT edit any *_test.go.

code_fault.description: (*Set).Subtract unconditionally walks the argument set a and deletes each element from s, so subtracting a large a from a small s does O(len(a)) work instead of O(len(s)).

ops_fault.description: Index search with a huge number of deleted series spends excessive CPU in uint64set Subtract because it scans the larger of the two sets unconditionally.
detection_keywords: high CPU in Subtract hot loop
index search slow with many deleted series

visible_context.issue_text: Subtracting one uint64 set from another gets very slow when the set being removed is much larger than the target; index searches over series with many deletions burn CPU in Set.Subtract.
error_logs: pprof: 71% of Subtract samples in uint64set.(*Set).Del via a.ForEach, work scales with len(a) even when len(s) is tiny
visible_context.notes: Real upstream optimization; profiling diagnosis injected as upstream context.
